content.title: Lady Vols basketball season ends in NCAA first round for third time ever
content.text: Updated March 20, 2026, 11:04 p.m. ETANN ARBOR, MI – Lady Vols basketball's season started and ended the same way: A loss to NC State.No. 10 seed Tennessee got into a hole early in the game and trailed by 15 points, and it was too much to overcome. The Lady Vols got within two points of the No. 7 seed Wolfpack in the third quarter, but couldn't sustain their momentum to tie or take the lead.Tennessee (16-14) fell 76-61 to NC State (21-10) on March 20, ending its season in the first round of the Women's NCAA Tournament for just the third time in program history. The only other years the Lady Vols lost in the first round were 2009 and 2019.Tennessee also went winless in the postseason for the first time in program history. The Lady Vols lost their only SEC Tournament game to Alabama.The 16 wins on the season tied the fewest wins in a season in program history, and it's only the second season ever in the NCAA era that the Lady Vols didn't reach 20 wins. The eight-game losing streak to end the season was the longest in program history.The only other season that happened, excluding the pandemic-shortened 2020-21 season, was the 2018-19 season when Tennessee went 19-13 in Holly Warlick's final season as head coach. That was also the only season the Lady Vols were seeded lower as a No. 11 seed.Talaysia Cooper led Tennessee with 24 points on 9-for-20 shooting and six rebounds. She also had three steals, two assists and four turnovers. Zee Spearman added 10 points and six rebounds.The Lady Vols opened the season with an 80-77 loss to NC State in Greensboro, North Carolina.Tennessee was without senior forward Janiah Barker, the team's second-leading scorer and top rebounder. Barker was out due to illness, according to the ESPN broadcast.Lady Vols basketball vs. NC State: Live score updates Tennessee trails 57-48 after third quarterThe Lady Vols got within two points of NC State with three minutes left in the quarter, but they couldn't sustain that momentum to take a lead.Tennessee outscored the Wolfpack 19-17 in the third, but still trailed 57-48 going into the fourth. Talaysia Cooper had a team-high 21 points on 8-for-16 shooting. The Lady Vols held NC State to 21.4% shooting from the field, but they sent the Wolfpack to the free throw line too much and they shot 10-for-10 from the line. Lady Vols chip away at lead, trail 46-39Tennessee outscored NC State 10-6 to open the third, and the Wolfpack only shot 1-for-9 while UT shot 4-for-8.Talaysia Cooper and Deniya Prawl both had five points, and Cooper drew a foul that led to the media timeout with 4:39 left in the third when Tennessee trailed 46-39. HALFTIME: NC State 40, Tennessee 29Tennessee recovered enough to stay in the game, but the Lady Vols couldn't get out of their own way at times. They gave up 10 points off six turnovers and settled for far too many 3-pointers, shooting 3-for-22 from deep.NC State shot 63% from the field and outscored Tennessee in the paint 24-14.Talaysia Cooper led the team with 14 points on 6-for-13 shooting with four rebounds. Zee Spearman added six points on 3-for-7 shooting. Lady Vols hang even with Wolfpack in second quarter behind Talaysia CooperTennessee and NC State both scored 10 points in the second quarter before the media timeout with 1:53 left. The Wolfpack led 36-29.Talaysia Cooper stayed hot in the second, scoring six points on 3-for-5 shooting. But Tennessee shot 29.4% overall in the second, including missing all eight 3-point attempts as NC State sat in a zone defense. Tennessee trails NC State 26-19 after first quarterAfter Kim Caldwell called timeout with 4:56 left in the first, Tennessee turned things around. The Lady Vols went on a 10-0 run to cut into the lead and trailed 26-19 after the first quarter.Talaysia Cooper led the team with eight points on 3-for-7 shooting, including 2-for-4 from 3-point range. Lady Vols trail by 15 at first media timeoutTennessee did not get off to a good start against NC State, which went on a 15-0 run to take a 19-4 lead at the media timeout with 4:56 left in the first quarter.The Wolfpack went 8-for-8 from the field, led by seven points from Zam Jones. They scored eight points off of five Tennessee turnovers. Janiah Barker out for Lady Vols vs NC StateSenior forward Janiah Barker was listed as out on the NCAA availability report for Tennessee's first round matchup. Barker was not on the initial report on March 19.Barker also participated in the open period of practice on March 19 and was one of two players at the press conference. The Lady Vol Radio Network said pregame that Barker was sick.When is Lady Vols vs. NC State in Women’s March Madness?Date: Friday, March 20, 2026Start time: 8 p.m. ETWhere: Crisler Center in Ann Arbor, MichiganWhere to watch Lady Vols vs. NC State in NCAA tournamentTV: ESPNStreaming: Fubo (free trial)Why does Tennessee have rematch with NC State in NCAA first round?The Lady Vols dropped from their projections of a No. 8 seed to a No. 10 seed, which left one option for placement that didn't set up an SEC matchup in the first or second round. The Women's NCAA Tournament now distributes "units," which are financial rewards for conferences based on how far teams advance.The units are distributed to conferences, so it made the most sense for the NCAA selection committee to prioritize the conference seeding principles in Tennessee's case.Lady Vols basketball 2025-26 schedule, TV timesNov. 4: NC State 80, Tennessee 77Nov. 7: Tennessee 97, ETSU 47Nov. 9: Tennessee 72, UT Martin 61Nov. 13: Tennessee 68, Belmont 58Nov. 20: Tennessee 85, MTSU 41Nov. 23: Tennessee 88, Coppin State 35Nov. 30: UCLA 99, Tennessee 77Dec. 3: Tennessee 65, Stanford 62Dec. 14: Tennessee 112, Winthrop 40Dec. 20: Louisville 89, Tennessee 65Dec. 22: Tennessee 89, Southern Indiana 44Jan. 1: Tennessee 76, Florida 65Jan. 4: Tennessee 73, Auburn 56Jan. 8: Tennessee 90, Mississippi State 80Jan. 11: Tennessee 85, Arkansas 50Jan. 18: Tennessee 70, Alabama 59Jan. 22: Tennessee 60, Kentucky 58Jan. 29: Mississippi State 77, Tennessee 62Feb. 1: UConn 96, Tennessee 66Feb. 5: Tennessee 82, Georgia 77Feb. 8: South Carolina 93, Tennessee 50Feb. 12: Tennessee 98, Missouri 53Feb. 15: Texas 65, Tennessee 63Feb. 17: Ole Miss 94, Tennessee 81Feb. 19: Texas A&M 82, Tennessee 74Feb. 22: Oklahoma 100, Tennessee 93Feb. 26: LSU 89, Tennessee 73March 1: Vanderbilt 87, Tennessee 77March 5: Alabama 76, Tennessee 64Why does Kim Caldwell make substitutions so often?Caldwell's system involves full-court pressing for 40 minutes. In order to keep players' legs fresh, Caldwell often subs in full lineups every two or three minutes. If Tennessee presses less in a game, she won't always sub five players at a time.Kim Caldwell's postseason recordKim Caldwell has never missed an NCAA Tournament as a head coach. She went to six straight Division II NCAA Tournaments at Glenville State and then took Marshall to its first NCAA Tournament since 1997 in her first season coaching in Division I.Caldwell is 34-12 overall in postseason games. She has won five conference tournaments, including the Sun Belt Tournament in her lone season at Marshall, and led Tennessee to the Sweet 16 in her first season.Tennessee women's basketball roster 2025-26Senior Janiah Barker – Forward, No. 0Senior Nya Robertson – Guard, No. 1Senior Jersey Wolfenbarger – Forward, No. 8Senior Zee Spearman – Forward, No. 11Redshirt junior Talaysia Cooper – Guard, No. 55Junior Alyssa Latham – Forward, No. 33Redshirt sophomore Kaniya Boyd – Guard, No. 4Freshman Lauren Hurst – Guard/Forward, No. 7Freshman Mya Pauldo – Guard, No. 12Freshman Mia Pauldo – Guard, No. 13Freshman Jaida Civil – Guard, No. 15Freshman Deniya Prawl – Guard, No. 25Cora Hall is the University of Tennessee women's athletics reporter for Knox News.
